title: Change the Image decode API wording / spec.
body: This is a follow up for #2037. The current wording in https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#dom-img-decode, point 3 states that if "this img element's current request changes or is mutated", then the promise should be rejected. This means that the basic case of img.src = "..."; img.decode().then(...); should reject the decode. This is due to the fact that https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html#updating-the-image-data states in point 4 that the algorithm to actually change the request has to be done via a microtask that runs, in this case, after the decode request has been issued. This means that the request is changed after the decode has been issued, which in turn means the decode has to be rejected. This isn't the intent of the API, so we should change the wording to allow for this case. Some suggestions (from @domenic, edited) are: - Have decode() queue a microtask to do all its work (including the initial checks, or perhaps just the current request check). This seems a bit like a band-aid, but maybe it is just a good alignment with 's existing use of microtasks - Introduce some new "src change pending" flag which we use to bypass the initial checks. I guess "pending request" is not actually this, as it isn't set until after the microtask starts [...] - Something else, perhaps inspired by [the current Blink implementation]. The current Blink implementation invalidates the request upon receiving a request for the src/srcset change, which queues the microtask to change the current request. This seems like an acceptable behavior. One contentious point is that if the src changes to the same value as before, the decode is invalidated. This seems OK. All other cases are handled "correctly", as in they are in line with the intent of the API.
